name: Honed
process: The sawn face is ground flat with bonded abrasives of progressively finer grit and stopped before it polishes. Travertine is filled first when a filled face is wanted; open-pore honing leaves the voids.
processSources: Molina E., Arizzi A., Benavente D., Cultrone G. (2020) 'Influence of surface finishes and a calcium phosphate-based consolidant on the decay of sedimentary building stones due to acid attack', Frontiers in Materials 7:581979, Tables 1 and 2, https://doi.org/10.3389/fmats.2020.581979 ('abrasives with progressively finer grain size without reaching a polished finish')

Dynamic Stone Tools (trade guide, undated), 'Grit progression by stone type: polishing sequences guide', https://dynamicstonetools.com/blogs/news/grit-progression-by-stone-type-polishing-sequences-guide

Natural Stone Institute (2022) Dimension Stone Design Manual, chapter 12 'Travertine' (Specification, Product Description, Technical Data), pp. 12-1 to 12-14, https://transparencycatalog.com/assets/uploads/greener-images/12-TRAVERTINE-2022.pdf, Product Description 4.1.5 and 11

abrasiveSequence.source: Dynamic Stone Tools (trade guide, undated), 'Grit progression by stone type: polishing sequences guide', https://dynamicstonetools.com/blogs/news/grit-progression-by-stone-type-polishing-sequences-guide
abrasiveSequence.conditions: the start of the marble sequence; trade practice; the grit scale is not named

stopsAt.source: Dynamic Stone Tools (trade guide, undated), 'Grit progression by stone type: polishing sequences guide', https://dynamicstonetools.com/blogs/news/grit-progression-by-stone-type-polishing-sequences-guide
stopsAt.conditions: 'a honed finish ends the sequence at 400 or 800 grit'; trade practice

definition.text: Honed: a satin smooth surface with little or no gloss.
definition.source: Natural Stone Institute (2022) Dimension Stone Design Manual, chapter 12 'Travertine' (Specification, Product Description, Technical Data), pp. 12-1 to 12-14, https://transparencycatalog.com/assets/uploads/greener-images/12-TRAVERTINE-2022.pdf, Product Description 4.1.2

Natural Stone Institute (2022) Dimension Stone Design Manual, chapter 12 'Travertine' (Specification, Product Description, Technical Data), pp. 12-1 to 12-14, https://transparencycatalog.com/assets/uploads/greener-images/12-TRAVERTINE-2022.pdf, Specification 6.2.5.2

glossGround.source: McDonell J.A., Kyle R.C. (Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co.) (1994) US Patent 5,282,900 'Nonwoven surface treating articles, system including same, and method of treating calcium carbonate-containing surfaces with said system', https://patents.google.com/patent/US5282900A/en
glossGround.conditions: marble test tiles ground with a 120-grade abrasive: 'less than 5 glossmeter reading at any angle'

glossWithGrit.text: While the grit falls to 320 the roughness drops steeply but the gloss hardly changes; after 320 the gloss rises steeply while the roughness changes little. Gloss follows roughness well in micritic limestones and marbles, less well in travertines.
glossWithGrit.source: Yavuz H., Ozkahraman T., Demirdag S. (2011) 'Polishing experiments on surface quality of building stone tiles', Construction and Building Materials 25:1707-1711, abstract as indexed (full text not read), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2010.10.016

arealRoughness.source: Molina E., Arizzi A., Benavente D., Cultrone G. (2020) 'Influence of surface finishes and a calcium phosphate-based consolidant on the decay of sedimentary building stones due to acid attack', Frontiers in Materials 7:581979, Tables 1 and 2, https://doi.org/10.3389/fmats.2020.581979, Table 2
arealRoughness.conditions: Sa, honed Travertino Amarillo, fresh and untreated; Leica VDM2000 videomicroscope; no filter is stated, so open pores are presumably included; Sz 1.11 mm

colour.text: Honing darkened and yellowed Travertino Amarillo against its saw-cut face: L* 65, a* 12, b* 31 against 69, 8, 17.
colour.source: Molina E., Arizzi A., Benavente D., Cultrone G. (2020) 'Influence of surface finishes and a calcium phosphate-based consolidant on the decay of sedimentary building stones due to acid attack', Frontiers in Materials 7:581979, Tables 1 and 2, https://doi.org/10.3389/fmats.2020.581979, Table 1
colour.note: the rows are in Substances/travertine.json, optics.measuredColour

voidTreatment.text: Travertine for horizontal use is usually filled with cement or epoxy similar in colour to the background.
voidTreatment.source: Natural Stone Institute (2022) Dimension Stone Design Manual, chapter 12 'Travertine' (Specification, Product Description, Technical Data), pp. 12-1 to 12-14, https://transparencycatalog.com/assets/uploads/greener-images/12-TRAVERTINE-2022.pdf, Product Description 4.1.5

voidTreatment.text: Filled and honed, and open-pore honed, are both sold.
voidTreatment.source: Travertino Romano Group (Guidonia Montecelio), 'Tivoli travertine quarries' (finishes listed: filled/honed, open pore honed, brushed, brushed open pore, antique, natural split), read 2026-09-26, https://www.travertino-romano.com/en/formation/tivoli-travertine-quarries

recommended.text: A honed finish is recommended for commercial travertine floors, with at least 20 mm of stone and an abrasion hardness of at least 10.
recommended.source: Natural Stone Institute (2022) Dimension Stone Design Manual, chapter 12 'Travertine' (Specification, Product Description, Technical Data), pp. 12-1 to 12-14, https://transparencycatalog.com/assets/uploads/greener-images/12-TRAVERTINE-2022.pdf, Product Description 8.1

photograph: Soft, broad reflections of windows and lamps, with no sharp image.
The colour a little paler and flatter than the same stone polished.
Open voids read as dark dots; filled voids as flush patches of a slightly different tone and sheen.

unverified.reason: No measured gloss of calcite stone honed to 400 or 800 grit was read.
No filtered (micro-scale) roughness of honed travertine or Crema Marfil was read; the Sa values above include pores and waviness.
